title: rosa communis var. hispidula
intro: Rosa communis var. hispidula, commonly known as the wild rose or dog rose, is a fragrant and thorny shrub native to Europe and Western Asia. This plant has been used for its medicinal and therapeutic properties for centuries, with potential health benefits including anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antioxidant effects, as well as helping to soothe digestive issues and calm nervous conditions. The therapeutic actions of Rosa communis var. hispidula include its ability to reduce inflammation, promote wound healing, and exhibit sedative properties, making it a popular ingredient in herbal remedies. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and essential oils, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions and potential health benefits.
